convertibility_reason: Uses external .mqh library (ClassWin.mqh) for GUI panel construction and event routing. Trading logic is simple but the panel UI and event handling are tightly coupled to the CWin/CClassWin framework, requiring manual extraction of trading logic from UI code.

custom_logic_notes: Signal is a simple bar-comparison system: compares current vs previous bar across Open, High, Low, Close, and 3 derived average prices ((H+L)/2, (H+L+C)/3, (H+L+C+C)/4). Each comparison increments either buy or sell counter (7 total). Autopilot mode: when buy_count > sell_count, opens BUY (closes SELL first if opposite position exists); when sell_count > buy_count, opens SELL (closes BUY first if opposite position exists). No SL/TP set on any trade. Manual BUY/SELL buttons bypass autopilot and signal logic. All trades use lot=0.01 with SL=0 and TP=0. The EA also has a GUI panel with Buy/Sell probability bars, BUY/SELL/CLOSE buttons, and an autopilot ON/OFF toggle.
python_conversion_notes: Trading logic is straightforward: 7-condition bar comparison signal with no SL/TP, fixed lot, and single-position management. The BUYorSELL() function is self-contained and easily ported to Python. Key complexity: (1) the autopilot toggle (on_trade flag) must be preserved as a runtime parameter; (2) position gate logic checks for existing position and closes opposite before entering—implement as check-then-close-then-open sequence; (3) no digit adjustment needed since SL/TP are zero; (4) GUI panel logic should be discarded—only extract BUYorSELL signal + autopilot execution + manual button equivalents as CLI parameters; (5) signal fires every tick with no new-bar guard, so backtest should use tick data for accurate fill modeling; (6) NormalizeDouble(lot,2) is redundant for fixed 0.01 but keep for consistency.
